recipes.name: French Orange Poached Pears (Poire Avec Orange)

steps.text: Combine orange juice, brown sugar, white sugar, vanilla extract, and cinnamon in a large saucepan over medium heat; bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolved. Place pears into syrup, cover, and simmer 1 hour and 15 minutes, flipping pears twice and spooning sauce over pears every 10 minutes.
Transfer pears to individual serving dishes. Continue cooking syrup, stirring often, until thickened, about 15 minutes, then stir in walnuts. Pour sauce over pears.

raw_recipe.headline: French Orange Poached Pears (Poire Avec Orange)
raw_recipe.description: This French orange poached pears (poire avec orange) recipe simply poaches pears in sweetened and spiced orange juice for a light, refreshing dessert.

recipeInstructions.text: Combine orange juice, brown sugar, white sugar, vanilla extract, and cinnamon in a large saucepan over medium heat; bring to a boil, stirring until sugar dissolved. Place pears into syrup, cover, and simmer 1 hour and 15 minutes, flipping pears twice and spooning sauce over pears every 10 minutes.
Transfer pears to individual serving dishes. Continue cooking syrup, stirring often, until thickened, about 15 minutes, then stir in walnuts. Pour sauce over pears.

review.reviewBody: This was absolutely delicious. I do not know why, but this recipe called to me to be poured over vanilla ice cream a la banana foster. I am so glad that I did. Although I did not change the recipe any, I did use an apple corer to core the pears (easier in my opinion). This also sliced them. One thing I would recommend though is use either less sugar or unsweetened orange juice. Otherwise it will be very sweet. All in all, a wonderful treat.

This was delicious. On the suggestion of another reviewer, I used much less sugar - half quantities. I was also skeptical about the amount of vanilla extract - I've never used a recipe that called for TABLESPOONS rather than teaspoons of vanilla. So I used half quantity, but on tasting the juice decided to add the other half. What a difference it made! The extra vanilla really balanced the cinammon. I would recommend preparing the recipe the night before serving because the pear flavor really comes through. If you are a ginger lover, add some chopped crystallized ginger. It really complements the other flavors. Definitely a winning recipe!
I didn't have orange juice so I used 1 cup Hungarian apricot brandy and 1/2 cup water instead. I also quartered the pears. I served them over vanilla ice cream. It was sweet but really yummy.
I substituted honey for the sugar and added in some cloves to the poaching liquid. I served it with coconut cream which helped cut the syrup.

I made this for dessert tonight, after French onion soup and roast chicken. What a perfect ending to a great meal! I used the Splenda brand brown sugar blend and skipped the white sugar, but still excellent! All that was left was the stem!

I quartered and cored the pears before cooking. They were so delicious on their own, but I also ate some with my morning oatmeal with a little of the syrup drizzled over. They would be awesome over waffles, pancakes or ice cream too! The tablespoon of vanilla really comes through in the final taste, and your house will smell great while the pears cook.
Amazing!!!Easy to make and absolutely wonderful to eat!! I am going to make this in summer with peaches and in fall, apples. Yum !!!!!!

Elegant, simple and delicious! I like the orange juice alternative to the alcohol-based simmering stocks. Was surprised by the call for 1*tablespoon* vanilla, so only used 1 teaspoon--seemed a nice balance with the orange and cinnamon and didn't overwhelm the flavor of the pear... Will make again tonight for my mother!!
So delicious! I love the transformation of the texture to; an almost gelatinous state. The orange French sauce really adds to the flavor and steps it up a notch.
Super easy, but elegant dessert. I will definitely make again! Delicious!
I made this a while back (like several years ago) but I still think about it. It is quite sweet and very decadent.
Delicious. I couldn’t eat a whole one so cut them up to top ice cream. Had extra sauce that I saved to top ice cream too.
Made this dish at Thanksgiving, everyone absolutely loved it and it was simple to make!!!
I made it and it was great, and the fancies thing I ever served, I really felt proud to serve it at my adult dinner party. Lol

The amount of sugar is too much for me. I suggest reducing the sugar. As written the sugar masks the natural sweetness of the orange and pears. I made these into little Halloween rats for fun. Thank you for the recipe.
This is so simple and yet elegant. Wonderful flavor, would make a nice company meal dessert served in champaine glasses. I will make again.
